title: Restauracja · co mówić
title_en: In a restaurant · what to say
note: Situations/chunk unit — the functional payoff of a2_food2. Fixed phrases, learned whole, no rule slides. Only FOUR genuinely new items: stolik, poleca (polecac), smaczne (neuter of the taught smaczny/smaczna), smacznego. Everything else is recycled: poprosze + accusative from a2_shopping_func, menu / rachunek / restauracja / kelner from A1, deser / danie / napoj / widelec / serwetka / smaczny / smaczna from a2_food2, czy mogE placic kartA and place kartA from a2_shopping_func. PATH-ORDER TRAP (found while writing): POOL was generated at the end of a2_dat_chunks, but in tree.json path_order a2_ordering_func sits at index 101 and a2_dat_chunks at 102 — i.e. AFTER this node. So nothing from a2_dat_chunks is legally available here: no smakuje mi, no nie smakuje mi, no podoba mi sie, no mi, no mnie. The obvious restaurant line 'Smakuje mi ta zupa' was therefore DROPPED even though it is in POOL, and 'it was delicious' is carried by Bylo bardzo smaczne / Wszystko bylo bardzo smaczne instead, which needs only past byc (taught) plus one new adjective form. a2_food2 at index 100 IS before this node and is fully available. TRAP 1 — ASPECT. zamowic is perfective and is not used anywhere. zamawiac is imperfective and IS in POOL, but only as an infinitive: zamawiam / zamawiasz are NOT in POOL, so under the every-form-taught rule using them would mean teaching a new present set. The whole zamawiac family was therefore dropped: poprosze already does the ordering job and is the phrase Dad will actually say. No perfective past anywhere; the only past forms used are bylo, byla, byl, all taught by past_byc. poprosze is kept on the same terms a2_shopping_func set — an unanalysable politeness word, never conjugated, no aspect or future content attached. polecac is imperfective and only ever appears as the 3sg poleca, inside a fixed question. TRAP 2 — POLITE ADDRESS, QUARANTINED. Co pan poleca? / Co pani poleca? are taught as two whole opaque questions. The learner is told one thing only, in plain English: Polish addresses a stranger with pan for a man and pani for a woman, so pick the one that matches the person. That is a lexical pick, not a system. NOWHERE does this pack decline pan/pani (no pana, panu, pania, panstwo), conjugate polecac (no polecam, polecasz, polecacie), contrast formal with informal (no Co polecasz?), or name the third person as a politeness device. No quiz item is a pan/pani/pana/panu four-way. As an escape route the unit also teaches Co jest dobre? — zero new words (co + jest + dobre are all taught), real spoken Polish, and it has no pan or pani in it at all, so Dad always has a version he can produce under pressure. TRAP 3 — TABLE FOR TWO, DROPPED ENTIRELY. Stolik dla dwoch osob needs dla (not in POOL at all), the genitive of a numeral, and osoba in the genitive plural — three untaught things in one phrase, and the virile counting behind it is B1. Stolik dla dwojga is worse. The function is not offered. Slide 1 tells the learner in English to hold up fingers, which is what actually happens in a restaurant doorway. 'How many people?' as a heard question was also dropped for the same reason. OTHER DROPS: 'w restauracji' (locative restauracji not in POOL — this is also why the title is Restauracja and not W restauracji); toaleta, karta dan, przystawka, glowne danie, poprosic, chcialbym (conditional), na wynos — all checked against POOL, absent, left out. The conjunction i IS in POOL now but is deliberately not used, so every list in the pack is two short sentences rather than one joined one. Real contrast the unit DOES teach, because both sides are already taught: Poprosze rachunek (restaurant bill, asked for) vs Poprosze paragon (shop till receipt, handed over) — quiz item 6.

intro.title: Getting a table — Czy jest wolny stolik?
intro.body:
A stolik is a table in a restaurant — the small table you sit at, not the big stół at home. It is the one new word on this slide.

Everything around it you already own. Czy jest…? is the same question you use in a shop, and wolny means free, not taken.

Czy jest wolny stolik? = "Is there a free table?" Ask this in the doorway, before you sit down anywhere.

Czy ten stolik jest wolny? = "Is this table free?" Use this one when you are standing beside a particular table and want to check. Point at it as you say ten.

A note on numbers. To say "a table for two" Polish needs a way of counting people that you have not met yet, and this unit is not going to open it. Hold up two fingers — every waiter in Poland understands that, and Czy jest wolny stolik? has already done the hard part.
intro.body_pl: Czy jest wolny stolik? Czy ten stolik jest wolny?

rows: in the doorway, before you sit
Dzień dobry. Czy jest wolny stolik?
Good day. Is there a free table?
the whole thing, from your side

intro.title: Ordering — Poproszę does all the work again
intro.body:
Nothing new here at all. The word you already use in a shop is the word you use at a table, and it is the whole of ordering.

Poproszę menu. — "The menu, please." Menu never changes its ending, whatever stands in front of it.

After that, put the thing you want straight after Poproszę, in the same form it takes after mam. Feminine words in -a swap to -ę: zupa → zupę, woda → wodę. Masculine and neuter words change nothing at all: deser, napój, widelec, talerz.

So the whole of ordering is one word plus the name of the thing. You do not need a verb for "order" and you will not be given one.
intro.body_pl: Poproszę menu. Poproszę zupę. Poproszę wodę. Poproszę deser.

rows: zupa → zupę, the same -ę as in mam zupę

examples.en: A soup, please. A water, please.

intro.title: Asking what is good — two versions, pick either
intro.title_pl: Co jest dobre? Co pan poleca? Co pani poleca?
intro.body:
Co jest dobre? = "What's good?" Every word in it is already yours. Co counts as neuter, so the adjective is dobre — the same -e as in To danie jest dobre. This version works everywhere and needs nothing new.

The fuller question uses poleca, which means "recommends". It belongs to the -a family you already produce in mieszka and czyta, so the ending is nothing new.

One thing to know, and then leave alone. Polish does not say "you" to a stranger. It uses pan to a man and pani to a woman — the two words you already have. So there are two versions of this question and your only job is to pick the one that matches the person in front of you:

Co pan poleca? — to a waiter.
Co pani poleca? — to a waitress.

Nothing else in the question moves. Learn the two as they stand and do not take them apart.
intro.body_pl: Co jest dobre? Co pan poleca? Co pani poleca?

rows: anyone — no pan or pani in it
The menu, please. What do you recommend?

examples.en: Excuse me, what do you recommend? (to a man)
— What do you recommend? — This dish is very good.
examples.pl: — Co pani poleca? — To danie jest bardzo dobre.

intro.title: Smacznego! — and saying it was good
intro.body:
Smacznego! is what Poles say to each other the moment food arrives, before anyone starts. English has nothing that fits — "enjoy your meal" is the nearest. The waiter will say it to you; anyone at your table will say it to you.

Take it whole. It is one fixed word, it never changes, and there is nothing inside it to work out. Dziękuję is a complete answer. If the other person is eating too, say Smacznego! straight back.

At the end you want to say it was good, and here you already have almost everything. Smaczny and smaczna are yours from the last unit. The third form is smaczne, and it is the one you use when you are not naming the thing:

Było bardzo smaczne. — "It was very tasty."
Wszystko było bardzo smaczne. — "Everything was very tasty."

Name the thing and the ending follows it, exactly as you already do: Zupa była bardzo smaczna. Deser był bardzo dobry.
intro.body_pl: Smacznego! Było bardzo smaczne. Wszystko było bardzo smaczne.

examples.en: Thank you. Everything was very tasty.
The soup was very tasty. The dessert was very good.
examples.pl: Zupa była bardzo smaczna. Deser był bardzo dobry.

intro.title: The bill — Poproszę rachunek
intro.body:
Rachunek is the bill at the end of a meal. Poproszę rachunek. is how you ask for it, and it is the only way you will need.

Watch the pair, because they are easy to swap. Paragon is the printed till receipt a shop hands you. Rachunek is what you ask a waiter for when you have finished eating. Different words, different places.

Paying is exactly what it was in the shop, so there is nothing new to learn:

Czy mogę płacić kartą? — "Can I pay by card?"
Płacę kartą. — "I'm paying by card."
Płacę gotówką. — "I'm paying cash."

And To wszystko, dziękuję. still ends the exchange, exactly as it does at the till.
intro.body_pl: Poproszę rachunek. Czy mogę płacić kartą? To wszystko, dziękuję.

rows: at the table, at the end
in a shop, at the till

examples.en: The bill, please. Can I pay by card?

quiz.prompt: You have just walked into a restaurant and want a table. You say:
quiz.explain: This is the same Czy jest…? you already use in a shop, with a new word on the end. Wolny means free, not taken.

quiz.prompt: You are standing beside one particular empty table. You say:
quiz.explain: Czy jest wolny stolik? asks whether they have any free table at all. When you are pointing at one, name it with ten and the adjective goes to the end.

quiz.prompt: The waiter is a man and you want his advice. You say:
quiz.explain: Pan is for a man, pani for a woman. Nothing else in the question changes — choose between those two words and you are finished.

quiz.prompt: You are speaking to a waitress. →
quiz.explain: Pani is the one for a woman. If you cannot remember which is which in the moment, Co jest dobre? does the same job and has no pan or pani in it at all.

quiz.prompt: You have just sat down and want to see what they have. You say:
quiz.explain: Menu at the start, rachunek at the end — the two ends of a meal, and both of them ride on Poproszę.

quiz.prompt: You have finished eating and want to pay. You say:
quiz.explain: Paragon is the printed till receipt a shop hands you. Rachunek is the bill you ask a waiter for at the end of a meal.

quiz.prompt: Your food arrives and the waiter says one word. He says:
quiz.explain: Smacznego is said before anyone starts eating. It is one fixed word, it never changes, and there is nothing inside it to work out.
Dziękuję is a complete answer. If the other person is eating too, you can say Smacznego! straight back instead.

quiz.prompt: The meal is over and you want to say it was good. You say:
quiz.explain: Smacznego comes before the food, never after it. Afterwards you say what it was like.
A czy question is a yes/no question, so the answer comes back with tak or nie, not with a request of its own.

quiz.prompt: The waiter asks whether you want anything else. You have finished. You say:
quiz.explain: The same phrase that closes a shop visit closes a meal. Every word in it is already yours.
Co counts as neuter, so the adjective takes the neuter -e: dobre. It is the same ending you already use in To danie było dobre.
